title: Suarez and others allow images adored as proximate terminus without directly adoring the exemplar
source_text: XLIII. At vero plures alii docent licitum & honestum esse imagines adorare non adorato simul exemplari, & ita ut ipsae sint proximus & integer terminus adorationis. Quo de numero est Franciscus Suarez, qui affirmat, licet verum sit imagines non posse adorari, nisi propter exemplar, nihilominus illas in se & proprie adorari posse, non adorato directe, & ut quod, exemplari. Tomo primo in tertiam Thomae, Disputatione quinquagesima quarta Sect. 5.
pass_a_gloss: But truly many others teach that it is lawful and honest to adore images with the exemplar not adored at the same time, and so that they themselves are the proximate and integral terminus of adoration. Of which number is Franciscus Suarez, who affirms that, although it is true that images cannot be adored except on account of the exemplar, nevertheless they can be adored in themselves and properly, with the exemplar not adored directly and as that-which. First tome on the third part of Thomas, Disputation fifty-fourth, section 5.
pass_b_english: Many disagree with Vasquez: images may be adored without simultaneously adoring the exemplar, as proximate terminus.
Suarez: images cannot be adored except because of the exemplar, yet can be adored in themselves and properly without directly adoring the exemplar as quod.
Cited: Suarez on ST III, disp. 54, sect. 5.

lemmas.gloss: with the exemplar not adored directly

choices.why: Scholastic contrast with ratio or propter quid.
